note: Prepared from the unit title and the trade's usual practice. An instructor must read and correct it, and mark it Ready, before it is opened for an intake.

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: Why do you hold a consultation with the client before a hair styling service?
options: To agree on the style the client wants and check that it suits their hair
To settle the price before the client has a chance to change their mind
To fill the time while the blow-dryer and the tongs are heating up
To sell the client as many styling products as possible that day

questions.stem: In hairdressing, what does hair 'texture' mean?
options: The number of hairs growing on each square centimetre of the scalp
How thick or thin each single hair is: fine, medium or coarse
How much natural oil the scalp makes during the day
How quickly the hair grows from one month to the next

questions.stem: A client has tightly coiled natural hair. Why does this hair type often feel dry?
options: The scalp's natural oil cannot easily travel down the coiled strands
Coiled hair has no cuticle layer, so it cannot hold on to any water
Coiled hair grows faster, so the ends are always newer and drier
Coiled hair makes less keratin protein than straight hair does

questions.stem: Which style usually suits a round face best?
options: A wide, full style with lots of volume over the ears
A short, rounded bob with a heavy, straight fringe
A style with height on top and less width at the sides
A flat, sleek style pulled tightly to the sides of the head

questions.stem: Kerry-Ann swims at the beach most weekends and has little time to do her hair in the mornings. What should the stylist suggest?
options: A style that needs daily heat styling with tongs to keep its shape
A silk press that she must keep away from sea water and sea breeze
A detailed up-style held with lots of spray and many hair pins
A low-upkeep style, such as braids or twists, that lasts for weeks

questions.stem: How do you carry out an elasticity test on the hair?
options: Slide your fingers from the ends of a strand towards the scalp
Look closely at the hair under a bright light to judge its shine
Gently stretch a few damp strands and see if they spring back
Rub a few strands between your fingers to feel how thick they are

questions.stem: During the consultation you see small open sores and crusts on the client's scalp. What should you do?
options: Carry on with the style, but keep all heated tools away from the sores
Do not do the service, and tactfully advise the client to see a doctor
Put a little styling oil on the sores so that they heal more quickly
Comb hair over the sores so that other clients do not notice them

questions.stem: Before using a pressing comb (hot comb) on a client, how should you test its heat?
options: Press it on a clean white towel or tissue and check that it does not scorch
Touch the teeth quickly with a wet finger and listen for a sizzle
Hold it close to the client's ear and ask whether the heat feels comfortable
Run it once through the client's hair and watch for any smoke

questions.stem: Before plugging in a blow-dryer, what should you check?
options: That the plug and cable are not damaged and your hands are dry
That the dryer is set on the highest heat so it warms up quickly
That the cable is long enough to wrap tightly round the handle
That the nozzle is taken off so that the air can flow more freely

questions.stem: A flat iron's cable is split and you can see the wires inside. What should you do?
options: Wrap the split part with tape and carry on using it with care
Use it only for short, quick styles until the end of the working day
Put it back on the shelf and let the next stylist decide what to do
Stop using it, label it 'Do not use' and report it to the supervisor

questions.stem: A hot curling tong touches a client's ear. The skin is red and sore but not broken. What is the right first aid?
options: Rub butter or cooking oil on the burn to soothe the skin
Hold ice directly on the burn until the area goes numb
Burst any blister that forms so the skin can breathe
Cool it under cool running water for 10 to 20 minutes

questions.stem: When curling close to the roots, why do you place a comb between the hot tong and the client's scalp?
options: To hold the section flat so that the curl comes out straighter
To protect the scalp from the heat of the tong and prevent a burn
To keep the comb warm so that it is ready for the next section
To stop loose hair from falling onto the client's face as you work

questions.stem: What is the main use of a nozzle (concentrator) on a blow-dryer?
options: To spread the air out gently so that natural curls keep their shape
To make the dryer quieter so that the client can hear you talking
To cool the air down so that the hair does not get too hot
To direct the airflow onto the section you are working on

questions.stem: When would you choose a diffuser for blow-drying?
options: To dry curly or coily hair while keeping the curls defined
To straighten thick, coarse hair quickly with a round brush
To dry the roots of very short hair as fast as possible
To give a very smooth and sleek finish to relaxed hair

questions.stem: Which brush is best for giving lift and a smooth curve at the ends during a blow-dry?
options: A paddle brush
A vent brush
A wide-tooth comb
A round brush

questions.stem: What is the correct way to detangle natural, coily hair before styling?
options: Start at the roots and comb quickly down to the ends with a fine comb
Brush the hair while it is dry with a bristle brush to loosen the knots
Work in sections from the ends up to the roots with a wide-tooth comb
Pull the knots apart with your fingers as fast as you can to save time

questions.stem: Why do you put a heat protectant on the hair before using a flat iron?
options: To make the hair dry faster so that the service takes less time
To add a colour to the hair that lasts until the next shampoo
To help reduce damage to the hair from the heat of the iron
To make the plates of the flat iron heat up more evenly

questions.stem: A client with fine, flat hair wants more volume. Which product would you put on the damp hair before blow-drying?
options: A heavy oil-based pomade
A light volumising mousse
A thick shea butter cream
A strong-hold shine serum

questions.stem: What is a shine serum mainly used for?
options: To give strong hold to an up-style for a whole day
To smooth frizz and add shine to the finished style
To clean build-up off the scalp between shampoos
To add lift and volume at the roots of the hair

questions.stem: Why should you use only a small amount of serum or oil sheen on fine hair?
options: Too much will weigh the hair down and make it look greasy
Too much will make the hair grow coarser over a few weeks
Too much will turn the hair a lighter colour in the sun
Too much will stop the hair from drying after a shampoo

questions.stem: When blow-drying hair smooth, which way should the airflow point?
options: Up the hair shaft, from the ends towards the roots
Straight onto the scalp, holding the dryer still
Down the hair shaft, from the roots towards the ends
Across the hair in any direction, moving quickly

questions.stem: Why is the hair divided into sections before blow-drying?
options: So that the client can see each part of the style in the mirror
So that less heat is needed and the dryer can be set to cold
So that each part is dried evenly and the stylist keeps control
So that product can be left off the parts that are already dry

questions.stem: What should you do to the hair straight after the shampoo, before the blow-dry starts?
options: Rub it hard with a towel to dry it as fast as possible
Leave it dripping wet so that it is easier to style
Brush it firmly from the roots while it is soaking wet
Blot it gently with a towel to remove the extra water

questions.stem: Why do you keep the blow-dryer moving and not hold it in one place?
options: To make the dryer use less electricity during the service
To stop the hot air from blowing on the other clients
To avoid overheating one spot of the hair or scalp
To make the motor last longer before it wears out

questions.stem: What is the 'cool shot' button on a blow-dryer used for?
options: To switch the dryer off quickly in an emergency
To blow dust out of the filter at the back
To set the shape by cooling the hair after heating
To dry wet hair faster than the hot setting can

questions.stem: Why should you clean the air filter at the back of a blow-dryer regularly?
options: So that the dryer blows cooler air during the service
So that air flows freely and the motor does not overheat
So that the dryer is lighter and easier to hold up
So that the nozzle fits more tightly onto the front

questions.stem: Why must the hair be completely dry before you use a flat iron or curling tong?
options: Wet hair is too heavy to fit between the plates of the iron
Wet hair makes the tool cool down and stop working at once
Heat on wet hair can boil the water inside it and damage the hair
Wet hair will make the finished curls come out much tighter than wanted

questions.stem: Which heat setting does fine or damaged hair need on a flat iron?
options: A lower heat setting, within the maker's range
The highest heat setting, to finish in one pass
Any setting, because fine hair is not harmed by heat
A higher setting than is used for coarse, thick hair

questions.stem: What does a 'silk press' do to natural hair?
options: Straightens it smoothly with heat, without using a chemical
Straightens it for good, using a chemical like a relaxer
Adds tight curls by setting the hair on small perm rods
Adds length by sewing extra hair onto the natural hair

questions.stem: Pressed (heat-straightened) natural hair goes back to its curl pattern in humid weather. What is this called?
options: Breakage
Porosity
Reversion
Shrinkage

questions.stem: Why do hydrogen bonds in the hair matter for heat styling?
options: They break with water or heat and re-form as the hair cools and dries
They break only with strong chemicals such as relaxers and perms
They hold the colour pigment inside the hair and fade when heat is used
They are found only in the scalp, not in the hair strand itself

questions.stem: When curling with a tong, how do you avoid 'fish hooks' (bent ends)?
options: Leave the ends out of the tong so that they curl on their own
Use the hottest setting so that the ends are set straight away
Hold the ends smoothly in the tong before winding up the rest
Spray the ends with water before each section goes in the tong

questions.stem: How is a cornrow different from a free-hanging plait?
options: A cornrow is twisted with two strands instead of being plaited
A cornrow uses only the ends of the hair, not the roots
A cornrow can only be done on hair that has been relaxed
A cornrow is plaited flat against the scalp along a parting

questions.stem: What is a two-strand twist?
options: A plait woven with three strands crossed under one another
A curl made by setting the hair around a foam roller
A section of hair pinned into a flat circle on the scalp
A section split in two and the parts wound round each other

questions.stem: A client wants a twist-out. When do you take down (unravel) the twists?
options: While the hair is still damp, straight after the twisting is done
When the hair is fully dry, so the curls hold their shape
After a shampoo, so that the twists come apart more easily
Before any product is put on, so there is no build-up

questions.stem: Why should the partings for box braids be neat and even?
options: So that the braids dry faster after the client washes them at home
So that less styling product is needed to hold each braid in place
So that the braids can be taken out later without any detangler
So that the braids look tidy and their weight is shared evenly

questions.stem: What is a Bantu knot?
options: A section twisted and wound into a small coil that sits on the scalp
A long, three-strand plait that hangs down from the crown of the head
A large bun pinned at the nape of the neck for a formal look
A curl formed by winding the hair around a hot curling tong

questions.stem: What does backcombing (teasing) do to the hair?
options: Smooths the cuticle so that the hair looks shiny and sleek
Removes knots from the ends of long hair before a shampoo
Takes out curl so that the hair hangs straight and flat
Pushes short hairs down to the roots to give lift and hold

questions.stem: Which of these gives the firmest grip for securing an up-style?
options: A U-shaped hair pin
A hair grip (bobby pin)
A large sectioning clip
A small crocodile clip

questions.stem: What is a French pleat (French roll)?
options: A vertical roll of hair pinned up the back of the head
A plait made with four strands that hangs down the back
A high ponytail at the crown, curled with a tong
A row of pin curls set flat along the nape of the neck

questions.stem: Why do you put a little hairspray or texture spray on very silky hair before an up-style?
options: To make the hair softer and more slippery to work with
To give the hair grip so that pins and shape hold better
To wash out any old products before you start pinning
To give the hair a darker colour for an evening event

questions.stem: What is padding (a hair 'doughnut') used for in an up-style?
options: To protect the scalp from the heat of the dryer
To give a bun a full, even shape and support
To hold the hair in place while it is shampooed
To soak up extra product from the client's hair

questions.stem: At the end of the service, why do you show the client the back of the style with a hand mirror?
options: So that the client can check that none of the hair pins are showing
So that the client can pay before they get up from the chair
So that the stylist can see the style from the client's side
So that the client can see and agree with the finished result

questions.stem: What advice helps a client keep a silk press or blow-dry for longer?
options: Wrap the hair or wear a satin bonnet at night and avoid humidity
Wash the hair every morning to keep it fresh and full of bounce
Sleep with the hair damp so that it keeps its shape through the night
Put heavy grease on every day to protect the style from the sun

questions.stem: How should brushes and combs be treated after each client?
options: Wipe them with a dry towel and put them back in the drawer
Remove the hair, wash them, then disinfect them as the maker says
Leave them in the disinfectant jar overnight with the hair still on
Rinse them under the tap and use them again for the next client

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What is the outer, protective layer of the hair shaft called?
Which protein is hair mainly made of?
What do we call the number of hairs growing on a given area of the scalp?
Which hair test is done by sliding the fingers along a strand from the ends towards the roots, to feel how rough it is?
What is the name of the natural oil made by the glands in the scalp?
What is the name of the small pocket in the skin that each hair grows from?
How many strands of hair are used in a basic plait?
What is the name of the plait that starts at the crown and picks up new hair into each cross as it moves down the head, lying on top of the hair?
Which face shape is thought of as the most balanced, a little longer than it is wide?
What is the name for hair loss caused by constant pulling from tight styles?
Which infection of the scalp, caused by a fungus, shows as round, scaly patches with broken hairs?
What are the small insects called that live on the scalp and lay eggs (nits) on the hair?
What is the French name for an up-style in which the hair is wound into a bun or knot at the back of the head?
What word describes curly or coily hair looking much shorter when dry than when it is stretched out wet?
On what document does the stylist write down the client's details, the service and the products used?

essays.stem: Describe how you would carry out a consultation and hair analysis before a styling service. Say what you would ask the client and what you would look at.
essays.modelAnswer: Greet the client, seat them at the mirror and put on a clean gown. Ask open questions: what style they want, what it is for, how they care for their hair at home, how much time they spend styling, and whether they have had chemical services such as a relaxer or colour. Ask about allergies and any scalp problems, and look at any pictures they bring. Then look at the hair and scalp: the curl pattern (straight, wavy, curly or coily), the texture (fine, medium or coarse), the density, the length and the condition. Do a porosity test and an elasticity test. Check the scalp for cuts, sores, infection or lice, and do not go ahead if you find any; advise the client to see a doctor. Look at the face shape and head shape. Agree the style, time and price, and write it all on the record card.
markingPoints: Asks open questions about the style wanted, the occasion, lifestyle and home care
Asks about past chemical services, allergies and scalp problems
Checks curl pattern, texture, density, length and condition, with porosity and elasticity tests
Checks the scalp for contraindications and does not go ahead if any are found
Agrees the style, time and price and records them on the record card

essays.stem: Explain how to use heated styling tools (blow-dryer, flat iron, curling tong and pressing comb) safely, for the client and for yourself.
essays.modelAnswer: Before use, check each tool: the plug, cable and casing must not be damaged, and the dryer filter must be clean. Use tools only with dry hands, away from water, and keep cables from trailing where people walk. Follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules. Put a heat protectant on the hair and make sure the hair is dry before using an iron or tong. Choose the lowest heat that works: less for fine, damaged or relaxed hair. Test a pressing comb on a white towel or tissue before it goes near the hair. Place a comb between the tong and the scalp, and protect the ears and neck. Keep the dryer moving and ask the client if the heat is comfortable. Rest hot tools on a heat-proof stand, never on the client or the chair. Switch off and unplug after use and let tools cool before putting them away. Report any fault and label the tool 'Do not use'.
markingPoints: Checks plug, cable and casing; dry hands, no water nearby, cables not trailing
Heat protectant on dry hair, and the lowest heat that works for the hair type
Tests the heat (for example a pressing comb on a white towel) before it touches the hair
Protects the scalp, ears and neck: comb under the tong, dryer kept moving, asks the client
Rests tools on a heat-proof stand, unplugs after use and reports faults

essays.stem: Describe the steps for a smooth blow-dry with a round brush on shoulder-length relaxed hair.
essays.modelAnswer: After the shampoo and conditioner, blot the hair with a towel and comb it through gently with a wide-tooth comb. Apply a heat protectant, and a light mousse or lotion if the client wants body. Rough-dry the hair on a medium heat until most of the water has gone. Divide the hair into four or more sections and clip them up. Start at the nape. Take a small mesh, no wider than the brush, place the round brush under it at the roots, and point the nozzle down the hair shaft from roots to ends while the brush turns and follows. Keep the dryer moving. Dry each mesh fully, then use the cool shot to set it. Work up the back, then the sides and top, lifting the top sections for volume. Relaxed hair is delicate, so use a medium heat and gentle tension. Finish with a little serum and check the balance in the mirror.
markingPoints: Prepares the hair: blots, detangles, applies heat protectant (and product if needed), rough-dries
Sections the hair and works from the nape upwards in small meshes
Points the nozzle down the hair shaft, moving brush and dryer together and keeping the dryer moving
Dries each mesh fully and cools it to set the shape
Uses gentle heat and tension for relaxed hair, then finishes and checks the balance

essays.stem: Describe how to prepare and straighten natural, coily hair with heat (a silk press) while keeping damage as low as possible.
essays.modelAnswer: Do a consultation and check the scalp. Shampoo with a moisturising shampoo and use a conditioner to soften the hair and reduce tangles. Detangle in sections with a wide-tooth comb, from the ends up to the roots. Apply a heat protectant to every section. Blow-dry each section on a medium heat with a comb attachment or brush to stretch the hair, keeping the dryer moving. When the hair is completely dry, divide it into small sections. Set the flat iron to the lowest heat that will straighten this client's hair, within the maker's range: fine hair needs less heat than coarse hair. Pass the iron slowly once or twice from roots to ends, with a comb just in front of it for a smooth result. Do not keep going over the same section. Finish with a very light serum. Advise the client to wrap the hair at night, wear a satin bonnet and keep it away from water and humidity.
markingPoints: Shampoos and conditions, then detangles in sections from ends to roots
Heat protectant on every section; blow-dries to stretch; hair fully dry before ironing
Uses the lowest heat that works for the hair texture, within the maker's range
Small sections, one or two slow passes only, with a comb guiding the iron
Light finish and aftercare: wrap, satin bonnet, avoid water and humidity

essays.stem: Describe how to create a two-strand twist-out on natural hair, from clean damp hair to the finished style.
essays.modelAnswer: Start with clean hair that has been conditioned and detangled. Keep it damp with a spray bottle of water. Divide the hair into sections and clip them away. Take one small section, apply a leave-in conditioner and a twisting cream or butter, and comb it through. Split the section into two equal strands and wind them around each other from the roots to the ends, keeping an even, gentle tension. Twist the ends firmly or coil them round a finger so they do not unravel. Repeat across the head, keeping the partings neat. Let the twists dry completely, either in the air or under a hood dryer on a low to medium setting. When they are fully dry, put a little oil on your fingers and unravel each twist gently, then separate the curls for fullness. Shape the style with your fingers or a pick and lift at the roots. Do not comb through the curls, as this causes frizz.
markingPoints: Clean, conditioned, detangled, damp hair divided into neat sections
Applies leave-in conditioner and twisting cream to each section
Splits each section into two strands and twists from roots to ends with even tension, ends sealed
Lets the twists dry completely before unravelling
Unravels gently with oiled fingers and separates and shapes without combing

essays.stem: Mrs Campbell is going to a wedding and wants a French pleat. Describe how you would create it.
essays.modelAnswer: Do a consultation and agree the look. The hair should be clean and dry; a smooth blow-dry or tong curl may be needed first. Brush the hair smooth and, if it is very silky, add a little hairspray or texture spray so that the pins will hold. Backcomb lightly at the crown for lift, then smooth the top surface. Brush all the hair across to one side of the back of the head and secure a row of crossed hair grips up the centre, from the nape to the crown. Then bring the hair back over the grips and roll it inwards to make a vertical fold. Tuck the ends in at the top. Secure the fold with hair pins pushed into the roll so that they do not show. Smooth any loose hairs. Show Mrs Campbell the back with a hand mirror and check she is happy. Finish with hairspray, keeping it away from her face.
markingPoints: Prepares the hair (clean, dry, smooth) and adds grip if the hair is silky
Light backcombing for lift, with the top surface smoothed
Row of crossed grips up the back of the head as an anchor
Rolls the hair over the grips into a vertical fold and secures it with hidden pins
Finishes neatly, checks with the client using a back mirror, sprays away from the face

essays.stem: Compare at least three finishing products (for example hairspray, shine serum, edge control or gel, and oil sheen). Say what each does, which hair it suits and how much to use.
essays.modelAnswer: Hairspray holds the finished shape. A light hold suits soft, moving styles and a firm hold suits up-styles. It is sprayed from about 25 to 30 cm away, with the client's face protected. Shine serum smooths frizz and adds shine. It suits straight, blow-dried or silk-pressed hair, but fine hair needs only a drop or two, because too much makes it look greasy. Edge control or gel smooths and holds the hairline and short hairs. It is used in small amounts with a soft brush, gently, so the edges are not pulled. Oil sheen adds a gloss to natural, relaxed or braided hair, and is sprayed lightly from a distance. For every product, follow the maker's instructions, ask about allergies first, and use the least amount that gives the result.
markingPoints: Hairspray: holds the shape; light or firm hold; sprayed from a distance with the face protected
Serum: smooths frizz and adds shine; very little on fine hair
Edge control or gel: smooths and holds the hairline; small amount, applied gently
Oil sheen: adds gloss to natural, relaxed or braided hair, sprayed lightly
Uses the least amount that works and follows the maker's instructions

essays.stem: Explain how a client's face shape, hair type and lifestyle affect the style you recommend. Give examples.
essays.modelAnswer: A good style suits the client's face, hair and daily life. An oval face is balanced, so most styles suit it. A round face looks longer with height on top and less width at the sides. A long face looks shorter with width at the sides or a fringe. A square face is softened by curls or waves around the jaw. Hair type matters too. Fine, thin hair suits styles with lift that are not too long, while thick, coarse hair may need layers or braids to control its bulk. Tightly coiled hair suits twists, braids or a twist-out, which keep it moist, while straight hair may drop a curl quickly in our humid weather unless it is set. Lifestyle is just as important. A nurse on long shifts may need a neat style that lasts, a student may want low cost and little upkeep, and a client who swims needs a style that can get wet.
markingPoints: Explains at least two face shapes and how a style balances them
Links hair texture, density or curl pattern to suitable styles
Mentions the humid climate or how well the hair holds a style
Links lifestyle (work, time, sport or budget) to the choice of style
Gives sensible examples throughout

essays.stem: Describe how to clean and disinfect your tools and work area after a styling service. Explain the difference between cleaning, disinfecting and sterilising.
essays.modelAnswer: Cleaning removes dirt, hair and product with detergent and water. Disinfecting uses a chemical disinfectant to kill most germs on a tool or surface that has already been cleaned. Sterilising kills all germs, including spores, for example in an autoclave. After each client, remove the hair from brushes and combs, wash them in warm soapy water and rinse them, then soak them in disinfectant for the contact time the maker gives. Rinse, dry and store them in a clean, covered container. When heated tools are unplugged and cool, wipe them with a disinfectant the maker allows. Put used towels and gowns in the laundry bin and use fresh ones for each client. Sweep up hair, and wipe the chair, workstation and mirror. Wear gloves for strong disinfectant, keep the area ventilated, and keep chemicals labelled and stored away. Throw away used single-use items.
markingPoints: Correct difference between cleaning, disinfecting and sterilising
Removes hair, washes and rinses tools before disinfecting them
Uses the maker's contact time, then rinses, dries and stores tools covered
Heated tools unplugged and cool before wiping; fresh towels; sweeps and wipes the workstation
Gloves and ventilation for chemicals; single-use items thrown away

essays.stem: What advice would you give a client to look after their hair at home, first after a heat-straightened style and then after braids or cornrows? Say why.
essays.modelAnswer: After a blow-dry or silk press, tell the client to wrap the hair or wear a satin bonnet or scarf at night, or sleep on a satin pillowcase. This cuts friction and frizz. Avoid water, sweat and humid air, which make the hair go back to its curl; carry an umbrella and use a shower cap. Use little heat between visits, and always with a heat protectant, to prevent damage. For braids or cornrows, keep the scalp clean with a light cleansing spray or diluted shampoo, moisturise the hair and scalp lightly, and cover the braids at night. Come back to the salon if the braids feel painful, itchy or too tight, or if bumps appear at the hairline, as tension can cause hair loss. Do not leave braids in too long, because new growth can matt at the roots. Book the next appointment and suggest suitable products.
markingPoints: Protect the style at night with a wrap, satin bonnet, scarf or pillowcase
Avoid water and humidity after heat styling; little heat at home, with a protectant
Braids: keep the scalp clean and moisturised and cover at night
Return if there is pain, itching, tightness or bumps; do not leave braids in too long
Rebook and recommend suitable products, giving reasons

practical1.title: Blow-dry and heat finish on different hair types
practical1.brief: Work as a group of 4 or 5 in the Centre's salon. Each member is the stylist for one client: a group partner or a model who has agreed. Between you, the clients must include at least one with natural, textured hair and one with straight, wavy or relaxed hair. Each stylist does a consultation and fills in a record card, then blow-dries the clean, damp hair in sections and finishes it with a flat iron or curling tong. When a member is not styling, they take turns as the client, the photographer and the hygiene checker, so that every member does each job. Photograph only the hair and the work area, never faces, unless the model agrees and the Centre allows it. Add the photos and record cards to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group when every style is finished and the stations are clean.
materials: Clients' hair shampooed, conditioned and towel-blotted
Round brushes, paddle brushes, wide-tooth combs and tail combs
Flat irons and curling tongs, with heat-proof stands
Heat protectant, light mousse and shine serum
A clean gown, towel and cape for each client
Disinfectant for tools and surfaces, and a laundry bin
photos: Each station set up, with tools checked and cables kept tidy
Each client's hair after detangling and sectioning
Blow-drying in progress, with the nozzle pointing down the hair shaft
The flat iron or tong in use, with a comb protecting the scalp
Each finished style from the back and the side
The stations cleaned and the tools disinfected or put away
checklist: Carried out and recorded a consultation, including a scalp check and hair analysis
Checked the tools, plugs and cables before use and kept cables tidy
Applied heat protectant and sectioned the hair neatly
Blow-dried with the airflow down the hair shaft, keeping the dryer moving
Chose a heat setting to suit the hair type and tested the tool first
Protected the client's scalp, ears and neck from heat
Finished style is smooth, balanced and as agreed with the client
Gave aftercare advice, then cleaned and disinfected the tools and station
safety: Check every electrical tool before use; never use it with wet hands or near water
Rest hot tools on heat-proof stands and unplug them after use
Test the heat before a tool touches the hair, and use a comb to protect the scalp
Stop and tell the assessor if a client has cuts, sores or signs of infection on the scalp
Keep the floor dry and clear of hair and cables

practical2.title: Cornrows or flat twists into a pinned up-style on natural hair
practical2.brief: Work as a group of 4 or 5. Each member styles one training head with textured (coily) hair, or a group partner or model with natural hair who has agreed. Each stylist detangles the hair, plaits at least four neat cornrows (or flat twists) from the front hairline back to the crown, and then gathers the rest of the hair and the ends into a neat bun or roll, secured with grips and pins. Members take turns to photograph each other's work, and to check one another's partings and tension. Photograph only the hair and the work area, never faces, unless the model agrees and the Centre allows it. Hand in once for the whole group when every style is finished and the stations are clean.
materials: Training heads with textured hair, on clamps (or models who agree)
Wide-tooth comb, tail comb and detangling brush
Leave-in conditioner, light moisturiser and light styling gel
Hair grips, hair pins and snag-free elastic bands
photos: The hair detangled and sectioned, with the tools set out
The partings marked for the cornrows or flat twists
The cornrows or flat twists finished, from the front and top
The bun or roll pinned, from the back
The finished style from both sides
The stations cleaned and the tools disinfected
checklist: Detangled from the ends to the roots, in sections, without pulling
Kept the tension even and firm but not tight, especially at the hairline
Cornrows or twists are neat, flat and of even size
Secured the bun or roll with grips and pins that do not show
Finished style is balanced and smooth, with no loose ends
Cleaned and disinfected the tools and left the station tidy
safety: Do not pull the hairline or braid too tightly; ask a live model if it is comfortable
Stop if a model has sores, bumps or signs of infection on the scalp, and tell the assessor
Fix training heads firmly in their clamps
Use pins and grips with care near the scalp and keep them off the floor
